non_gpio_roles.condition: reboot / dfu commands; DTCM token checked before all application peripheral initialization
non_gpio_roles.description: Both reboot and dfu request NVIC_SystemReset (SYSRESETREQ/SFTRESET). The dfu path first disconnects TinyUSB and writes a DTCM token; the early token check then branches to ROM. The application does not drive NRST or BOOT0 via GPIO. RM0433 §8.4.2, Figure 43 documents the internal reset generator and its specified minimum pulse; that controller effect is distinct from the measured external waveform. At P2:10 (NR), the owner captured a physical button press and software reboot, including approximately 26 µs near zero during reboot. The schematic connects NRST through R1 (330 ohm) to SYS_RESET feeding camera DVP_RST (J2 pin 6) and TFT LCD_RESET (J3 pin 3); these downstream lines and dfu were not measured. The role retains no GPIO assignment. ROM pin configuration is outside this source audit and software DFU-entry reliability remains separately unresolved.

bench_observations.result: Rigol MHO984 capture at external P2:10 (NR): approximately 3.3 V at rest; physical button held NR low for 157.5 ms. Software reboot stayed near zero for approximately 26 µs. Other recorded intervals were approximately 114 µs from falling edge to 1.65 V during recovery, approximately 524 µs from start of rise to 3.0 V, and return to approximately 3.3 V around 1 ms.
bench_observations.limits: These intervals have different cursor endpoints and describe the external contact, not internal MCU reset duration. dfu, downstream TFT/camera reset lines and the cause of the recovery shape remain unmeasured. Acquisition/cursors were saved on the Rigol; raw export is unconfirmed.

No SDMMC initialization, reads or writes in application. PC8 is actively used for TIM3_CH3, so a board SD D0 connection is still a shared connection, not proof of an observed malfunction.

Only HSE and HSI are requested in SystemClock_Config. No LSE or RTC initialization found.

unconfigured_features.state: No application GPIO assignment to an external VBUS switch, overcurrent input, USB ID input or ULPI bus. USB roles are forced by the configuration. External 5 V host wiring remains a physical design requirement, not software-regulated power.

coverage.method: Read all targeted pin initialization/driving paths and searched every tracked firmware src/include file plus platformio.ini and the TinyUSB patch script for GPIO/HAL peripheral/clock/reset operations, direct register access and compile-time branches. Reconciled source definitions with call order and error/diagnostic paths. This is a static source audit, not a build or bench test.
diagnostic_and_conditional_coverage: Heartbeat and fatal Error_Handler use the same six GPIO outputs; early clock failures may prevent later peripheral setup.
outputs_init configures DAC analog pins, sequential pins and PC8 even when later DAC/PWM initialization fails non-fatally.
Handbrake mappings, direct overrides and test_axis all feed both PC8 PWM and the USART2 pedal stream; PWM driver checks s_hb_pwm_ok.
USART2 handshake/warmup/baud/reset/error paths retain PA2/PA3 AF configuration.
tud_mounted changes console buffering; PA9/PA10 remain configured as USART1.
usb_status reads controller registers; usb_kick and usb_stall affect host processing without assigning additional GPIO.
USE_FULL_ASSERT only adds an empty assert_failed; no conditional pin assignment.
DFU early ROM branch skips all app GPIO initialization; ROM internals are not app source assignments.
exclusions: STM32Cube framework/HAL weak MSP implementations were not exhaustively vendor-source-audited; no project MSP override exists. Relevant GPIO mux configuration is explicit in application source.
PlatformIO platform/framework versions are unpinned in this baseline; software startup/framework defaults are not promoted to fixed board assignments.
firmware-stm32/tools/esp32s3_uart_bridge is firmware for an optional external ESP32-S3, not the STM32 image. Host flash scripts do not define runtime STM32 GPIO assignments.
MCU/package capability tables and WeAct wiring are supplied by separate source audits.
findings: Nineteen explicit GPIO assignments plus two HSE oscillator contacts; port-clock enables do not reserve every contact on that GPIO port.
PA9/PA10 never switch to GPIO inputs on USB mount at this baseline; console remains a mirror/command source.
Actual USB roles contradict stale comments at main.c lines 709–710 and tusb_config.h lines 47/63; macros and configured functions are authoritative.

The bring-up heartbeat touches five pins in addition to PE3. Shared onboard nets, especially PD13/QSPI IO3 and PC8/microSD D0, must be recorded as source/drawing overlaps; no electrical malfunction is established here.
